title: A Semi-Automatic Approach to Developing a Large-Scale POS Tagged News Corpus for Urdu, a Low-Resource Language
abstract: The development of a large-scale, Part-of-Speech (POS) tagged corpus for Urdu, a morphologically rich and low-resource language, remains a significant challenge due to the scarcity of annotated linguistic data. This paper presents a semi-automatic approach to creating a comprehensive Urdu POS-tagged dataset, addressing the limitations of existing resources. The dataset, named MM-POST (Mushtaq & Muzammil POS Tagged) corpus, comprises 119,276 words/tokens drawn from 2,871 sentences across 75 online BBC Urdu news articles. These articles span seven diverse domains: General, Finance, Entertainment, Politics, Health, Sports, and Science, ensuring broad coverage of linguistic patterns. The tagging process combines the automated tagging capabilities of the Center for Language Engineering (CLE) POS Tagger with rigorous manual annotation, resulting in a high-quality and domain-sensitive corpus with a vocabulary size of 9,395 unique tokens. The study provides a detailed analysis of the corpus construction process, including tagging methodology, tagset design, domain-wise distribution, and corpus characteristics. The MM-POST corpus supports various NLP tasks such as Named Entity Recognition, Information Retrieval, Text Classification, and serves as a benchmark resource for training and evaluating Urdu POS taggers. By preserving syntactic structure, the dataset enables both token- and sentence-level text processing. Additionally, the paper reviews the evolution of Urdu tagsets and highlights prior machine learning-based POS tagging efforts. This work not only contributes a valuable linguistic resource for Urdu but also establishes a scalable framework for developing corpora in other low-resource languages. Future extensions include automated tagger development and Named Entity annotation to enhance the corpus’s applicability across NLP applications.

title: PatternForge: A Multi-Agent Generative AI Framework for Catalog-Driven Orchestration Across Enterprise CRM and Hyperscaler Cloud Platforms
abstract: Multi-agent generative AI deployments inside enterprises increasingly straddle two opinionated platform stacks at once: a Customer Relationship Management (CRM) system that owns the business object model (Salesforce, Microsoft Dynamics, HubSpot) and a hyperscaler cloud (Amazon Web Services [AWS], Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud Platform [GCP]) that owns the compute and model substrate (AWS Bedrock, Azure OpenAI, GCP Vertex). The orchestration patterns that make these deployments work, sequential pipelines, hierarchical supervisors, peer collaboratives, blackboards, and the rest, are reinvented by every team because no published catalog describes them at the level of granularity required for engineering reuse. We present PatternForge, a five-agent generative AI framework that turns a curated catalog of seven orchestration patterns into a deployable artifact. A Pattern Selection Agent (PSA) maps a structured task specification to a candidate pattern using a learned scorer over historical orchestrations; a Coordination Topology Agent (CTA) instantiates the chosen pattern as a typed message-bus topology; a Hyperscaler Adapter Agent (HAA) compiles the topology against AWS, Azure, or GCP primitives; a CRM Integration Agent (CIA) materialises the business object bindings against Salesforce or Dynamics; and a Pattern Evaluation Orchestrator (PEO) measures the realised orchestration against a multi-dimensional pattern-quality score Lambda. Evaluated on 37,400 orchestration tasks across three enterprise scenarios (lead triage, dispute resolution, renewal forecasting) over a 90-day controlled Continuous Integration / Continuous Deployment (CI/CD) pipeline, PatternForge achieves a pattern-selection F1 of 0.913, a Lambda score of 0.904 averaged across the seven patterns, a 68.4% reduction in median time-to-first-completed-task relative to a single-agent baseline, and a CRM-write integrity beta of 0.993 across 374,000 business-object writes. Single-agent ablation confirms each component contributes independently. All quantitative results are simulation-derived: every dataset is synthetic, every CRM write targets sandbox tenants, and no production CRM workload informed the evaluation; live-tenant validation remains the primary open problem.

title: Measurement of the Turbulent Channel Superoperator Acting on Single-Photon Polarization States Employing Quantum Process Tomography
abstract: Quantum process tomography (QPT) allows for the estimation of the quantum superoperator by performing multiple measurements using different input states. In this work, we estimate the superoperator that characterizes free-space propagation through atmospheric turbulence. For that, we propose the use of a fiber-based projective measurement station and a heralded single photon source to implement a proof-of-concept QPT device. We present a theoretical analysis of the setup and perform an experimental QPT of the atmospheric turbulence quantum channel acting on the polarization state for 5 different turbulence conditions. Our tests conclude that turbulence has a negligible impact on the polarization state of the photons transmitted through the channel, obtaining a probability for the identity operator close to 95% in all the turbulence conditions measured.

title: Alternating Bias Assisted Annealing Influences Amorphous Alumina Structure in Superconducting Quantum Resonators
abstract: Superconducting qubits (SQ) are favorable technology for quantum computing due to their macroscopic nature, coherence times, and gate speeds [1]. Materials synthesis and processing methods for SQs are common to fabrication in the semiconductor industry, promising easy scalability. Josephson junctions (JJ) are critical components of SQs and consist of a thin dielectric layered between two superconducting electrodes [2]. The prototypical JJ is an Al/AlOx/Al sandwich structure, as aluminum forms a thin, self-limiting oxide [2, 3]. Amorphous alumina (a-AlOx) has also seen widespread adoption as a dielectric in semiconducting devices due to favorable properties such as high breakdown fields and low leakage currents [4]. Aluminum oxidation follows Cabrera-Mott (CM) mechanisms, where adatom-induced fields drive Al-ion diffusion towards the surface [3]. Pappas et al. introduced alternating bias assisted annealing (ABAA), an electrical processing technique to tune JJ resistance [5]. ABAA applies alternating voltage pulses, below the JJ breakdown field but above the CM field, hypothesized to facilitate ionic diffusion and anneal the oxide. Via scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM), they demonstrated that ABAA induces a measurable change on the Al electron energy loss near-edge structure (EELS-ELNES), suggestive of potential changes in bonding and homogenization of the oxide [5]. Junction resistance with ABAA can be tuned to a narrow distribution, improving device performance [6]. Iaia et al. studied the influence of ABAA in thicker a-AlOx layers in superconducting resonators designed to study two level system defects (TLS) in the amorphous dielectric [7]. They note pronounced impact of ABAA applied and measured at mK temperatures (cryogenic alternating bias stimulation, CABS) on TLS behavior, which are reversible when the device is annealed to 10 K. In this work, we investigate the influence of ABAA on a-AlOx film structure using 4D STEM fluctuation electron microscopy (FEM). Synthesis and processing of the device is described in Iaia et al. [7]. Briefly, a ∼50 nm thick a-AlOx layer was synthesized via thermal atomic layer deposition (ALD), which differs from conventional a-AlOx growth in JJs. ABAA processing was applied with ±100 MV/m fields at 353 K over 30 hours. STEM sample thickness was controlled between 0.4 – 0.7 λEMFPAlOx⁠. 4D STEM experiments were performed at 300 kV on the Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory TEAM I, collected with a Dectris Arina detector, with a 1.2 mrad and 2 pA probe to minimize beam damage [8]. Thickness was calculated for each real space position based on the transmitted intensity of the diffraction zero-beam using a vacuum dataset for reference. The variance was normalized for thickness at each pixel and averaged across each row of diffraction patterns. Several datasets were collected, aligned, normalized, and averaged to improve statistics. Variance profiles are compared as a function of depth to understand a-AlOx medium range order across the device thickness. Figure 1 shows FEM analysis of a resonator. Fluctuation electron microscopy (FEM) variance was calculated using the Vr method for each pixel [9]. Variance is a metric which tracks how speckle intensity as a function of k fluctuates across a dataset [10]. Speckles originate from individual ordered atomic clusters in the amorphous material aligned on Bragg conditions [10]. A low variance is suggestive of a lower speckle-contrast amorphous halo with little fluctuation across the dataset, or a more uniform and amorphous structure. In contrast, a higher variance suggests stronger speckle contrast intensity fluctuations, with sources arising from both discrete speckles and changes across the dataset, or a more heterogeneous and ordered amorphous material. Figure 1 compares FEM normalized variance profiles between the as-made (AM) and ABAA devices, and Figure 2 isolates the peak variance values at ∼3 and ∼7 nm-1 as a function of distance from the TiN electrode. In the AM device, a pronounced decrease in the variance is observed near the TiN interface, suggesting a substantial reduction in amorphous structural order. This variance reduction extends several nm into the film. We speculate this may be attributable to TiN interfacial effects during the initial stages of the ALD growth. Datasets collected with different cross-sections, probe currents, shorter dwell times, and different scan geometries all show comparable TiN interfacial features, so we believe this effect is not attributable to electron or ion beam damage [8]. The ABAA-treated device shows only a modest variance reduction near the TiN interface. This suggests that ABAA increases the a-AlOx ordering near the interface. While the a-AlOx structure as a function of depth is more homogeneous after ABAA, the a-AlOx structure near the TiN interface can be thought of as more heterogeneous, peppered with well-ordered atomic clusters. We interpret this change as ABAA-induced ionic diffusion allowing the oxide to find more stable configurations [4,5]. ABAA thus offers a straightforward means to modify both the structure and properties of ALD AlOx layers inside devices [11]. Overview of spatially-resolved FEM measurements. A 4D STEM dataset is depicted by a virtual brightfield (vBF) image (top left). Each diffraction pattern’s variance is calculated, normalized based on the pixel thickness, and averaged across each row. Variances are compared as a function of depth in the AlOx layer. A representative diffraction pattern is shown (top right), with rings corresponding to maxima in the variance. Spatially resolved, normalized variance plots are shown for the as-made (bottom left) and ABAA (bottom right) devices with colors corresponding to locations depicted by the vBF colorbar. FEM comparisons between AM and ABAA devices. The AM device shows reduced variance near the TiN interface, mostly mitigated via ABAA processing.

title: Laboratory Demonstration of Phase-Time Encoding Quantum Key Distribution System with Multimode Delay Interferometer
abstract: Abstract We report on the adaptation of a commercially available fiber-based quantum key distribution (QKD) system with phase-time encoding to free-space operation. The proposed approach minimizes architectural modifications by replacing the single-mode receiving interferometer with a free-space multi-mode delay interferometer, enabling efficient detection of spatially distorted quantum states typical for atmospheric channels. Several interferometer configurations are experimentally investigated, and a multi-mode Michelson interferometer with polarization routing is identified as the optimal solution in terms of interference visibility, loss, and alignment robustness. The impact of chromatic and modal dispersion on phase-time interference is analyzed and shown to be manageable under realistic system parameters. A laboratory QKD experiment demonstrates stable operation with a quantum bit error rate of about 4.5% and a secret key rate of hundreds of bits per second, confirming the feasibility of extending fiber-based QKD platforms to free-space links.

title: Enhancement of fidelity using combined environment-assisted measurement and weak measurement strategies in hybrid communication
abstract: Abstract In this work, we discuss a strategy to enhance the robustness in a noisy environment of an asymmetric bidirectional hybrid quantum communication (ABHQC) through the combined use of environment-assisted measurement (EAM) and weak measurement (WM) techniques. In this protocol, we utilize EAM during the entanglement distribution stage and further modify the original communication scheme by applying WM in the final step of the communication process. By varying the strength of the WMs, we achieve a balance between the total fidelity and the success probability. Numerical findings indicate that with the applications of EAM and WM, the proposed scheme achieves superior performance compared to the unprotected ABHQC protocol.

title: AI-Induced occupational uncertainty as a multi-level challenge: reconciling human-centered values with automation in tourism and hospitality
abstract: This study examines AI-induced occupational uncertainty in the tourism and hospitality industry. A qualitative multi-level critical synthesis that combines critical reflection with narrative synthesis was applied to examine the pervasive effects of AI-induced job insecurity across individual, organizational, familial, and societal dimensions. The objective is to problematize the efficiency narrative of AI and uncover hidden socio-technical costs. AI adoption creates a double-edged sword effect, where operational gains offset psychological stress, familial relational strain, and deepening societal inequality. This study contributes a novel four-level synthesis framework and advocates for agile policy interventions, including participatory co-design, targeted reskilling, and universal social protections. By shifting the discourse from technical implementation to human dignity, this research provides a holistic diagnostic tool for industry leaders and policymakers to align technological innovation with the core human-centric values of hospitality.

title: Hamm-Grams: An Algorithm for Mining Regular Expressions of Bytes
abstract: Malware poses a critical and ever-evolving threat, and robust and effective systems for detecting and classifying malware are of essential importance. $n$-grams features are among the common static features used in effective machine learning systems for malware, but these features are inherently brittle. We propose an algorithm for constructing more robust features, hamm-grams, which are a special class of regular expressions having a fixed length and single-character wildcards. We devise an efficient algorithm for finding common hamm-grams using a new locality-sensitive hash designed to produce collisions among pairs of small Hamming distance and a clustering within hash buckets to place wildcards. We then demonstrate the advantages of these features in malware classification and detection tasks.

title: Cheap Code, Costly Judgment: A Case Study on Governable Agentic Software Engineering
abstract: Generative AI is shifting software engineering from a practice organized around scarce implementation effort toward one organized around abundant, low-cost code production. This shift changes the central engineering problem: not whether AI can generate useful code, but how engineers organize architectures, tools, evidence, and feedback loops so that AI-mediated development remains inspectable, correctable, and maintainable. We study this problem through a first-person case study: a 12-week development effort in which a single expert software engineer used frontier AI coding agents to build a document accessibility remediation system. The empirical record comprises 88 contemporaneous field notes, 420 KLOC of production code, and 1.16 MLOC of tests, lints, supporting documentation, and agent tooling. From this record, we develop a candidate middle-range theory of governance conversion, expressed as a process model explaining how high-velocity agentic implementation becomes governable. The model explains how agentic implementation velocity surfaces recurring structural failure classes, and how engineering judgment sustains velocity by converting those failures into durable governance mechanisms. In contrast to existing governance models that derive controls from known obligations, governance conversion explains how controls are discovered from failures that become visible only during agentic work. We use our model to make testable predictions and to describe implications for software engineering research and practice.

title: How Ethos and Pathos Appeals Resonate in Reader Interpretations of Social Media Messages
abstract: Rhetorical strategies and their influence on audiences are often studied through social media posts and comments. However, this focus overlooks the universal audience, which is the majority of readers who remain silent and do not explicitly express how a message affects them. This study investigates how two classical modes of persuasion, ethos and pathos, resonate in the silent audience's interpretations of meaning. Using a dataset of social media sentences paired with human-written interpretations, we label both sources for ethos and pathos and assess whether these rhetorical appeals are preserved. Our analyses show that interpretations diverge from the original sentences in 30% of cases, with rhetorically charged content eliciting greater variability than neutral content. We further find that ethos and pathos in original sentences can predict audience attitudes toward the author, underscoring the subtle ways rhetoric shapes perception beyond visible engagement.

title: Retrieved Images as Visual Thought: Training-Free Multimodal In-Context Learning for the Open-vs-Closed Gap
abstract: Recent work on Thinking with Images makes vision a dynamic part of reasoning, but does so through generation: the model invokes external tools, synthesizes code, or imagines new imagery, each at the cost of a tool protocol, brittle code, or an expensive training pipeline. A fourth route makes vision dynamic without generating anything, by retrieving labeled exemplar images and reasoning over them, yet it remains underexplored despite being train-free. We present ReVisIT, a train-free framework that realizes this retrieval-based route by treating each retrieved image-label pair as a unit of visual thought. ReVisIT combines structured class definitions, per-query multimodal retrieval of exemplars, and alternating user/assistant injection of those exemplars before joint multi-attribute decoding, and degrades gracefully to whichever components a task admits. On VL-ICL Bench Fast Open MiniImageNet, Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B with ReVisIT reaches 98.5% at 4-shot, statistically indistinguishable from the 72B LLaVA-OneVision SOTA (98.7%) on this near-saturated task at about 1/2.4 the parameters, while the same backbone without the scaffold sits at chance. The turns layer alone adds 26.1 points to GPT-4.1 on free-form concept induction (Bongard-OpenWorld), and the full stack yields a 4-6 point macro gain across three backbones on MAAC-Bench, a new license-clean 27-class, 5-attribute benchmark, significant by paired bootstrap on the curator-derived attributes. Component analysis shows that retrieval-plus-turns is the universal lever while structured definitions are need-adaptive, and that 83% of the retrieval gain comes from retrieval quality rather than from the presence of exemplars. MAAC-Bench is released with a rubric-grounded LLM verification protocol that replaces author spot-check on subjective attributes.

title: Vitality-Aware Compression for Efficient Image-to-Shape Diffusion Transformers
abstract: We propose the first compression approach for image-to-shape Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) that substantially reduces model size while preserving geometric fidelity. Despite remarkable progress in 3D shape generation, large DiT-based models remain computationally prohibitive in resource-constrained settings. Furthermore, it is difficult to directly transfer existing diffusion model compression strategies developed for different domains to 3D generation, and prior 3D efficiency approaches focus primarily on inference speed rather than backbone compression. To address this limitation, we build a geometry-aware compression framework tailored to image-to-shape DiTs. Guided by the observation that 3D DiT layers exhibit non-uniform importance for geometry synthesis, we introduce a vitality-guided framework integrating structured pruning, adaptive quantization, and targeted fine-tuning. Our method achieves up to 66% model-size reduction across state-of-the-art image-to-3D models while maintaining synthesis fidelity comparable to full-sized counterparts. This highlights the potential of our framework as a plug-and-play solution for efficient 3D shape generation across diverse models.

title: Software Between Quantum and Machine Learning - and Down to Pulses
abstract: Contemporary quantum computing platforms remain, in essence, programmable physical systems whose control is typically mediated through unitary gate abstractions. While such abstractions provide a uniform interface, they obscure important aspects of the underlying hardware and may limit the exploitation of its full capabilities. Direct operation at the control-pulse level offers a more expressive and physically faithful paradigm, enabling, for instance, the implementation of tailored error-mitigation and optimisation strategies. However, this increased expressivity comes at the cost of greater quantum software development complexity, necessitating structured and accessible tooling. We present a software framework, integrated within the QML-Essentials package, that extends quantum machine learning (QML) methodologies to encompass pulse-level modelling. By embedding quantum optimal control techniques within a QML setting, our approach enables the seamless combination of gate-based and pulse-level representations. The framework provides a comprehensive suite of modelling and analytical capabilities. In particular, we introduce composable ansatz constructions based on interchangeable building blocks, and support for end-to-end optimisation of pulse parameters. Motivated by the central role of quantum Fourier models, we further incorporate a range of Fourier-analytic diagnostics, complemented by extended measures of entanglement. All performance-critical components are implemented in a high-performance environment using JAX and supported by a dedicated quantum simulator. Taken together, the framework facilitates reproducible and systematic investigations, while bridging the conceptual and practical divide between abstract circuit models and hardware-aware optimisation. It provides a robust foundation for future developments at the intersection of QML and quantum control.

In particular, we introduce composable ansatz constructions based on interchangeable building blocks, and support for end-to-end optimisation of pulse parameters. Motivated by the central role of quantum Fourier models, we further incorporate a range of Fourier-analytic diagnostics, complemented by extended measures of entanglement. All performance-critical components are implemented in a high-performance environment using JAX and supported by a dedicated quantum simulator. Taken together, the framework facilitates reproducible and systematic investigations, while bridging the conceptual and practical divide between abstract circuit models and hardware-aware optimisation. It provides a robust foundation for future developments at the intersection of QML and quantum control.

title: Who Gets the Reward & Who Gets the Blame? Evaluation-Aligned Training Signals for Multi-LLM Agents
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) in multi-agent systems (MAS) have shown promise for complex tasks, yet current training methods lack principled ways to connect system-level evaluation with agent- and message-level learning. We propose a theoretical framework that unifies cooperative game-theoretic attribution with process reward modeling to transform system evaluation to agent credit to response-level signals. Unlike prior approaches that rely only on attribution (Shapley) or step-level labels (PRM), our method produces local, signed, and credit-conserving signals. In success cases, Shapley-based credit assignment fairly allocates outcomes across agents and is refined into per-message rewards that promote cooperation while discouraging redundancy or sabotage; in failure cases, first-error localization yields repair-aware preferences that penalize harmful steps while rewarding corrective attempts. The resulting signals are bounded, cooperative, and directly compatible with reinforcement- or preference-based post-training, providing a unified and auditable pathway from global evaluation to local supervision in LLM multi-agent training. Our contribution is conceptual: we present a theoretical foundation and training signals, leaving empirical validation for future work.

title: Quantum Harmonic Neural Networks: Application and Determination within the Context of Physics-Informed Neural Networks and Comparative Anomaly Detection
abstract: At the juncture of quantum-defined systems and classical digital structures, cybersecurity and computing are at an inflection point where both domains converge. This thesis examined the intersection of quantum information science and artificial intelligence, focusing on quantum harmonic analysis and physics-informed neural networks (PINNs). The research approach evaluated data and system behavior from a scientific, experimental perspective. Comparative studies were conducted to assess the proposed hypothesis. Specifically, the research question explored machine learning architecture and artificial intelligence design components in which PINN integration was engineered to support high mathematical precision and anomaly detection within a cybersecurity setting. The study involved coded experimentation using designated AI structures enhanced with simulated quantum processing, producing quantitative output for analysis and scientific interpretation. Methodologies were employed to formalize experimentation with a Geometrically Coherent Quantum Harmonic Neural Network (GCQHNN) and an enhanced physics-informed neural network. The experiment evaluated statistical variability and compared the proposed networks with classical machine learning models and related algorithms when challenged by known and unknown cyberattack vectors.

title: 3rd International Data Analytics and Machine Learning Conference DATAMACLEA’26 Full Texts Book
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is increasingly integrated into the core of economic, technological, andorganizational systems, fundamentally altering how value is created, labor is distributed, andproductivity is optimized. From AI-assisted software development pipelines to data-driven decisionmaking in corporate operations, intelligent systems are emerging as key drivers of efficiency andinnovation across industries. Yet, these transformations prompt critical economic reflections: Whichhuman-led tasks can be responsibly automated? What are the measurable benefits and hidden costs ofdelegating functions to AI? And how can institutions maximize value generation while maintainingadaptability and accountability? DATAMACLEA’26 welcomes empirically grounded and forwardlooking contributions that investigate these questions through technical insight, sectoral analysis, andreal-world application.At the same time, the growing adoption of AI technologies across sectors is unlocking new forms ofeconomic efficiency, operational resilience, and scalable innovation. From intelligent documentationand simulation systems to decision-support tools and remote service platforms, AI-powered solutionsare enabling organizations to optimize processes, reduce resource waste, and enhance outcome quality.These tools not only assist professionals in managing complex tasks but also generate measurable valueat the institutional, national, and global levels. DATAMACLEA’26 encourages contributions thatexamine how such AI-enabled innovations reshape economic models, improve productivity, and drivevalue creation across diverse domains, including healthcare, software, education, finance, and beyond.

title: Operationalizing the Motivated Intruder: A Codebook-Guided Inference Framework for Semantic Input Privacy in LLMs
abstract: The integration of LLMs into professional and personal workflows creates a semantic leakage vector, where sensitive data is exposed through contextual quasi-identifiers rather than explicit identifiers. We demonstrate that conventional syntactic sanitization (Regex/NER) is fundamentally insufficient for this threat model. To address this, we propose a codebook-guided privacy gateway, an architecture that operationalizes the GDPR's motivated intruder test into executable chain-of-thought logic. We evaluate this framework using a high-fidelity reference model to isolate logical validity from hardware constraints, validating results against a multi-stage human-annotated ground truth ($N=127$) to eliminate model-preference bias. Our findings are threefold. First, deductive inference outperforms pattern matching: the gateway achieves a 90% risk neutralization rate for trade secrets, significantly outperforming baseline methods which neutralize less than 5%. Second, privacy is a compute-bound task: sanitization efficacy correlates linearly ($r=0.985$) with chain-of-thought token volume, mapping a significant inference gap in current local models on consumer-grade hardware. Third, we identify the semantic coupling limit: a structural boundary in technical domains where robust privacy and high utility are mutually exclusive. This study establishes that effective input sanitization requires a shift from deterministic filtering to probabilistic, deductive inference.

title: Consumer Perception and Preferences towards AI Chatbots: An Empirical Study of E-Commerce Users in Ludhiana
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) chatbots have become a defining feature of the online shopping experience, reshaping the way e-commerce platforms communicate with and serve their customers. This study examines consumer perception, trust, and attitude toward AI chatbots in the context of online retail, and identifies the key factors that drive their preference and adoption among shoppers. An analytical research design was adopted, with primary data gathered through a structured questionnaire administered to 145 respondents from Ludhiana who had prior experience using AI chatbots while shopping online. Respondents were selected through random sampling, and the resulting data were examined using mean analysis and exploratory factor analysis. The findings indicate that consumers hold a broadly favourable view of AI chatbots, rating them positively for their helpfulness, ease of use, and convenience during the purchase process. Attitudes toward chatbot usage were equally encouraging, pointing to a growing willingness among consumers to rely on AI-driven assistance while shopping online. Trust, while moderately high overall, was tempered by lingering concerns over data privacy, security, and the reliability of chatbot responses. Exploratory factor analysis further revealed three underlying dimensions shaping chatbot adoption: User Acceptance, Perceived Convenience, and Behavioural Intention. Taken together, the results suggest that while AI chatbots are increasingly seen as valuable shopping companions, e-commerce businesses must continue to invest in stronger data security, deeper personalization, and more responsive design if they are to fully earn consumer trust and sustain long-term adoption. Keywords: Consumer Perception, Trust, Attitude, AI Chatbots, Consumer Preferences, Customer Satisfaction, E-commerce

title: Diagnosing AI Transformation in Consulting Engagements: The Balanced Automation Framework
abstract: Consulting engagements for AI-driven transformations frequently fail not because of technology, but because consultants lack a reliable way to diagnose and improve a client's readiness for human-AI collaboration. This paper provides that tool: the Balanced Automation Framework (BAF). The BAF is a deployable diagnostic that changes how AI engagements are run. Instead of relying on generic AI advice, consultants can use the BAF to systematically assess client capabilities, design targeted interventions for competency development, and structure a phased implementation that aligns with the client's specific context. This shifts the engagement from a technology-centric deployment to a capability-building partnership, materially increasing the probability of successful client transformation.

title: Scaling Model Size and Zero-Shot Cross-Lingual Transfer Performance in English Intermediate-Task Training
abstract: Intermediate-task training---fine-tuning a pretrained model on an intermediate task before fine-tuning again on the target task---often improves model performance substantially on language understanding tasks in monolingual English settings. We investigate whether English intermediate-task training is still helpful on non-English target tasks. Using nine intermediate language-understanding tasks, we evaluate intermediate-task transfer in a zero-shot cross-lingual setting on the XTREME benchmark. We see large improvements from intermediate training on the BUCC and Tatoeba sentence retrieval tas Research goal: How does the scaling of model size affect the zero-shot cross-lingual transfer performance of English intermediate-task training, as measured by F1 scores on the XTREME benchmark? title: Data-Consistency Loop SMOTE: A Closed-Loop Over-sampling Algorithm for High-Dimensional Imbalanced Data
abstract: Class imbalance is a pervasive challenge in machine learning, often leading to biased classifiers that perform poorly on the minority class. Although the Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) is widely used to mitigate this issue, its blind linear interpolation mechanism frequently introduces noisy samples and causes boundary blurring, failing to preserve the underlying distribution of the original data. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a novel over-sampling framework named Data-Consistency Loop SMOTE (DCL-SMOTE). Unlike traditional unidirectional sampling approaches, DCL-SMOTE establishes a self-adaptive, closed-loop iteration system driven by a "generation -> consistency check -> correction -> re-generation" workflow. The proposed algorithm evaluates each synthetic candidate through multi-dimensional consistency checkers encompassing probability distribution, spatial geometry, and manifold structure. Samples failing the evaluation are dynamically adjusted via gradient-based optimization in the correction module or discarded to trigger a feedback mechanism that adaptively refines the sampling weights of the baseline minority instances. Theoretical analysis demonstrates that the closed-loop feedback and self-healing mechanism effectively ensure that the generated samples conform strictly to the authentic minority distribution. This framework provides a robust and mathematically rigorous solution for pattern recognition and classification tasks in high-dimensional imbalanced domains.

title: An Improved SMOTE Oversampling Algorithm Based on a Multi-Strategy Voting Mechanism
abstract: Classifying imbalanced data remains a critical challenge in machine learning, as standard algorithms often favor the majority class and compromise the classification accuracy of the minority class. The Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) alleviates this issue by interpolating new samples linearly. However, its uniform generation strategy frequently introduces noisy data and blurs class boundaries. To address these limitations, this paper proposes an improved SMOTE algorithm based on a multi-strategy voting mechanism, termed Data-voting SMOTE. Unlike traditional approaches that rely on a single geometric model, the proposed method concurrently deploys three distinct generation strategies: standard linear interpolation, Gaussian perturbation center expansion, and three-point recombination centroiding. To ensure the quality of the synthesized data, a multi-indicator evaluation framework is established to quantify the spatial properties of each candidate sample based on density security and distance harmony. A majority voting mechanism then filters these candidates, accepting the final synthetic sample only when a consensus is reached among the strategies. This collaborative approach significantly enhances sample diversity while preserving sharp decision boundaries, thereby effectively reducing noise generation and improving the generalization performance of classifiers on imbalanced datasets.

title: Rule-chain SMOTE: An Oversampling Method Based on Rule-chain Inference Systems
abstract: Classifying imbalanced datasets remains a critical challenge in machine learning, as traditional classifiers tend to favor the majority class. The Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) mitigates this by generating synthetic instances through linear numerical interpolation between minority examples. However, this geometric approach often ignores the underlying logical relationships and business rules between features, leading to the creation of unrealistic "ghost samples" and poor handling of mixed-type data. To address these limitations, this paper proposes Rule-chain SMOTE, a novel oversampling methodology that replaces traditional numerical interpolation with a logical rule-chain inference system. Instead of filling space blindly, the proposed method treats sample generation as a chain-deduction process. By selecting and slightly perturbing core root features from real minority samples, the algorithm triggers a sequence of interconnected deterministic or probabilistic rules to sequentially deduce and complete the remaining features. This topological inference mechanism ensures that the generated samples strictly adhere to the intrinsic causal relationships and manifold constraints of the data. Rule-chain SMOTE naturally accommodates mixed-type features without losing statistical meaning through forced continuous encoding. The theoretical analysis demonstrates that the method significantly improves the logical soundness and interpretability of synthetic data while effectively preserving class boundaries, offering a robust and explainable framework for imbalanced learning.

title: A Contrastive Boundary Push SMOTE Over-sampling Algorithm for Imbalanced Data Learning
abstract: Class imbalance is a pervasive challenge in machine learning, where classifiers often bias toward the majority class due to the skewed distribution of data. The Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) alleviates this by interpolating synthetic instances within the minority class space. However, traditional SMOTE frequently generates samples that invade the majority class region, leading to severe class-overlapping and blurred decision boundaries. To address this limitation, this paper proposes a novel over-sampling method named Contrastive Boundary Push SMOTE (CBP-SMOTE). The core idea of CBP-SMOTE is to explicitly integrate the philosophy of contrastive learning into the data generation process. Specifically, after synthesizing a baseline instance, the algorithm identifies its nearest neighbor in the majority (negative) class space and constructs a push vector. By leveraging a distance-based feedback mechanism, the baseline instance is explicitly pushed away from the negative class representation space. This mechanism effectively sharpens the decision boundary and suppresses the overlapping effect. Theoretical and procedural analyses demonstrate that the proposed algorithm significantly clarifies class boundaries while maintaining the diversity of the minority class, thereby enhancing the generalization performance of classifiers on imbalanced datasets.

title: Multi-View SMOTE: Separate Generation and Alignment for High-Dimensional Imbalanced Multi-View Learning
abstract: Multi-view learning has emerged as a powerful paradigm in machine learning, where objects are characterized by multiple heterogeneous feature subsets or data sources. However, the ubiquitous class imbalance problem significantly undermines the classification performance in real-world multi-view applications. Traditional synthetic minority over-sampling techniques (SMOTE) are primarily designed for single-view data and fail to handle the complex structural correlations across different views. Directly applying single-view SMOTE to each view independently disrupts the alignment and cross-view consistency of the synthesized data, while feature concatenation severely exacerbates the curse of dimensionality. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a novel over-sampling framework named Multi-view SMOTE. The proposed algorithm decomposes the multi-view over-sampling process into a separate generation stage and a joint alignment stage. In the first stage, raw synthetic minority samples are independently generated within each distinct feature space using localized topological interpolation, preserving the specific characteristics of each individual view. In the second stage, a multi-view alignment mechanism is established by mapping all views into a unified lower-dimensional latent subspace. Cross-view consistency is enforced by minimizing the discrepancy among the projected representations of the minority class. A consensus representation is subsequently synthesized in the latent space and back-projected to the original view-specific spaces via pseudo-inverse reconstruction, ensuring that the final synthetic samples are perfectly aligned across all views. Theoretical formulations validate that Multi-view SMOTE effectively prevents semantic misalignment while mitigating the curse of dimensionality. The proposed framework provides an efficient, robust, and highly interpretable data-augmentation solution for imbalanced multi-view classification tasks.

abstract: МЕТОДИ ПІДВИЩЕННЯ ТОЧНОСТІ КЛАСИФІКАЦІЇ ДАНИХ НА ОСНОВІ АНСАМБЛЕВИХ МОДЕЛЕЙ МАШИННОГО НАВЧАННЯ Анотація.У статті досліджено методи підвищення точності класифікації даних на основі використання ансамблевих моделей машинного навчання в умовах оброблення багатовимірних та різнорідних інформаційних вибірок.Актуальність дослідження зумовлена необхідністю підвищення ефективності функціонування інтелектуальних інформаційних систем аналізу даних у задачах підтримки прийняття рішень, що застосовуються у сфері кібербезпеки, медичної діагностики, економічного прогнозування, технічного моніторингу та інших прикладних галузях.Зростання обсягів структурованих і неструктурованих даних, наявність шумів у вибірках та складність нелінійних залежностей між ознаками обумовлюють потребу у використанні сучасних методів підвищення точності класифікації на основі інтеграції результатів роботи декількох базових алгоритмів машинного навчання.У роботі запропоновано підхід до побудови stacking-ансамблю, який забезпечує інтеграцію результатів роботи моделей Random Forest, Gradient Boosting та багатошарової нейронної мережі з використанням метакласифікатора узагальнення результатів прогнозування.Проведено експериментальне дослідження ефективності запропонованого підходу на еталонному наборі даних Breast Cancer Wisconsin Dataset із використанням процедури кросвалідації та стандартних метрик оцінювання якості класифікації, зокрема точності класифікації, precision, recall та F1-міри.Отримані результати експерименту показали підвищення точності класифікації ансамблевої моделі у межах від 0,8% до 3,1% порівняно з окремими базовими алгоритмами машинного навчання, що підтверджує ефективність застосування stackingпідходу для задач класифікації багатовимірних даних.Наукова новизна отриманих результатів полягає у розробленні підходу до інтеграції моделей різної алгоритмічної природи у складі stacking-ансамблю для підвищення точності класифікації даних шляхом зменшення дисперсії прогнозу, систематичної похибки та ризику перенавчання моделі.

title: CA-LIME: A Collinearity-Aware LIME Framework for Reliable and Interpretable Explanations in Healthcare AI
abstract: In clinical tabular models, correlated biomarkers can make local explanations unstable even when predictive performance appears acceptable. This paper presents CA-LIME, a collinearity-aware extension of LIME built to address that failure mode directly. Five variations of CA-LIME Vanilla reference, VIF, PCA back projection, Ridge, and ElasticNet allow us to investigate how various correlation-control strategies alter explanation behavior. ILPD, Kaggle liver, a combined ILPD + Kaggle liver cohort, and heart stroke are the four dataset configurations on which we test the system. Existing validated ILPD/stroke assets are reused, and the same workflow is extended to the new liver parameters for consistency. With an emphasis on local interpretability, stability, clinical plausibility, and practical application, we also contrast CA-LIME with SHAP as the baseline explanation. Across settings, CA-LIME retains clinically meaningful feature emphasis and shows stable local behavior under correlated inputs. The findings clarify the remaining validation and deployment constraints while supporting CA-LIME as a decision-support explanation layer.

title: HOW ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE CAN TRANSFORM BUSINESS DECISION-MAKING AND STRATEGY DEVELOPMENT FOR AGRIBUSINESSES
abstract: In today's environment, artificial intelligence (AI), a set of technologies that mimic individual aspects of human thinking and behavior, is evolving into a powerful tool for supporting corporate management decisions. It enables companies to assess not only their current status but also formulate long-term strategies based on predictive models. Using the example of Agrofirm Svoboda CJSC, we propose a comprehensive model for using AI to improve the validity of management decisions, forecast key financial indicators, manage risks, conduct strategic planning and scenario modeling, and generate reports, forecasts, and possible scenarios online, facilitating the work of specialists. Overall, this article examines the importance of AI in improving the efficiency of agricultural production and proposes promising areas for its development, combining the latest technologies with the current conditions and needs of agricultural producers. This will enable Agrofirm Svoboda CJSC to apply innovative management approaches, making the company a leader in its industry, and AI will become a key data provider for strategic decisions.

title: Computational Complexity in Timed Argumentation Frameworks
abstract: Timed Argumentation Frameworks (TAFs) allow taking into account the availability of arguments and attacks in abstract argumentation. We propose a new reasoning approach for TAFs, where a standard Dung-style AF can be associated with each timepoint. We show that, although this framework is more expressive than Dung's framework, our approach does not lead to an increase in computational complexity for most reasoning problems and classical extension-based semantics.

title: Models of Legal Protection for Works Created with Involvement of Artificial Intelligence
abstract: The research focuses on the legal mechanisms for protecting works created using artificial intelligence (AI) technologies, taking into account their creation specifics and the degree of human creative involvement. The subject of the study is the system of legal mechanisms for protecting such works considering their creation features. The aim of the study is to develop theoretical and methodological foundations for a differentiated approach to legal protection of creative works created using AI technologies, and to formulate proposals for improving legislation in this area. The study hypothesizes the need to abandon the binary model of legal regulation (“protected or not protected”) in favor of a differentiated approach to determining the scope of protection depending on the degree of human creative participation and the level of AI system autonomy. The authors methodology includes formal legal, comparative legal, system-structural methods, and legal modeling. Based on the analysis of Russian and foreign legislation, doctrinal approaches, and judicial practice, the research justifies classifying AI works into three categories: those with predominant human creative contribution, hybrid works, and those with minimal human creative input. The study develops a system of criteria for evaluating the originality of algorithmically generated works (statistical uniqueness, result unpredictability, semantic coherence, aesthetic/functional value). A three-tier model of legal regulation for using protected works in machine learning processes is promoted, along with specific proposals for improving Russian intellectual property legislation considering modern technological challenges: amendments to Article 1228 of the Civil Code regarding criteria for the creative nature of an author’s activity when using AI; to Article 1259 — on the specifics of AI works’ legal regime; to Article 1274 — on free use of works for machine learning purposes; to Article 1286 — on licensing peculiarities for using works in machine learning; and introducing a new paragraph to Chapter 71 of the Code regulating rights to works created with minimal human creative participation (15-year protection period, indication of AI application).

title: Improving Cypher Query Generation from Natural Language using Reinforcement Learning with Large Language Models
abstract: This study addresses the automated generation of Cypher queries from natural language expressions for graph databases, systematically analyzing the impact of various training strategies and data augmentation techniques on model performance. Although Large Language Models (LLMs) demonstrate significant potential in natural language-to-query tasks, their generalization to unseen schemas and structural accuracy remain critical challenges. In this context, the study investigates the contributions of Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT), Reinforcement Learning (RL), and cross-domain training strategies utilizing relational database (SQL) data to the Text-to-Cypher task.

title: Enhanced Transformer Powered Time-Series Anomaly Detection via Contrastive Embedding and Unified Discrimination
abstract: This paper presents an enhanced Anomaly Transformer for unsupervised anomaly detection in multivariate time series. We introduce a contrastive embedding module that refines the input embedding by optimizing a lightweight MLP with an InfoNCE objective, where positive pairs are pulled closer while negative pairs are pushed apart in the feature space. We further propose Unified Discrimination at the decision stage, which unifies reconstruction error and association discrepancy into a single anomaly score. Experiments on four large-scale benchmarks (SMD, PSM, MSL, and SMAP) demonstrate consistent performance gains over the Anomaly Transformer baseline, improving Precision and F1-score while maintaining high Recall, with an average F1-score of 0.9554.

title: A Lyapunov-Guided Post-Action Shield for Stability-Aware Deep Reinforcement Learning
abstract: This paper proposes a Lyapunov-guided post-action shielding mechanism for deep reinforcement learning (DRL) controllers under bounded actuation disturbances. In addition, an energy-safety requirement is formulated as a one-step energy threshold constraint that keeps the predicted next-state energy proxy within a prescribed limit, using a bounded-disturbance worst-case check. Simulation results show that the proposed mechanism substantially reduces constraint violations under actuation noise while preserving the nominal policy behavior whenever possible.

title: Physics-Informed Imitation Learning for Resilient Autonomous Driving
abstract: Imitation learning has emerged as a promising paradigm for autonomous vehicle control. However, existing policies often suffer from severe covariate shift and lack explicit stability guarantees in closed-loop trajectory tracking. This paper proposes an adaptive Lyapunov-constrained imitation learning framework for vehicle trajectory tracking. To address the covariate shift problem, we explicitly embed a discrete-time kinematic bicycle model into the policy training process. This differentiable physical prior enables propagation of the nominal tracking error and allows a global Lyapunov decay constraint to be directly employed on the policy optimization via an Actor-Critic architecture. To prevent the overly aggressive penalization near the reference trajectory, we introduce a state-dependent adaptive decay rate that relaxes the constraint for small errors while strengthening it under large deviations. As a result, the proposed method achieves both high tracking precision and strong recovery from model uncertainties and disturbances. Extensive experiments in interactive traffic environments demonstrate that the proposed method significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in collision avoidance and disturbance rejection.

title: Practical demonstration of high-accuracy electronic structure on a quantum computer
abstract: Quantum computing offers a promising path toward accurate electronic structure calculations, especially for systems where classical methods face limitations. However, most quantum demonstrations to date have focused on simplified systems, lacking the quantitative precision required for direct comparison with experiment. In this work, we present a method tailored for implementation on existing and near-term quantum hardware. Our focus is on predicting a quantity that can be directly compared with experiment, enabling a meaningful benchmark of quantum hardware for chemical applications. We use a compact representation that is achieved through physically motivated simplifications of the wavefunction, reflecting a general strategy of adapting the representation to known properties of the system, even though the degree of simplification is system-dependent. We validate this approach by computing the total energy of neutral helium using the Quantinuum H1-1 ion-trap quantum computer, enabling us to determine the ionization potential to within true chemical accuracy of the experimental value. This represents a meaningful step toward practical quantum computational chemistry and establishes a framework for benchmarking future quantum hardware using real-world chemical systems.

evidence.title: Practical demonstration of high-accuracy electronic structure on a quantum computer
evidence.abstract: Quantum computing offers a promising path toward accurate electronic structure calculations, especially for systems where classical methods face limitations. However, most quantum demonstrations to date have focused on simplified systems, lacking the quantitative precision required for direct comparison with experiment. In this work, we present a method tailored for implementation on existing and near-term quantum hardware. Our focus is on predicting a quantity that can be directly compared with experiment, enabling a meaningful benchmark of quantum hardware for chemical applications. We use a compact representation that is achieved through physically motivated simplifications of the wavefunction, reflecting a general strategy of adapting the representation to known properties of the system, even though the degree of simplification is system-dependent. We validate this approach by computing the total energy of neutral helium using the Quantinuum H1-1 ion-trap quantum computer, enabling us to determine the ionization potential to within true chemical accuracy of the experimental value. This represents a meaningful step toward practical quantum computational chemistry and establishes a framework for benchmarking future quantum hardware using real-world chemical systems.

title: BiCAT: bidirectional cross-attention for asynchronous heterogeneous multi-source trajectory association
abstract: In recent years, multi-source, multi-target trajectory association is critical for air traffic management and intelligent transportation systems. Yet prevailing methods rely on rigid temporal alignment and hand-crafted rules; they deteriorate under cross-modal asynchrony, heterogeneous measurements, and high-density scenes. This paper presents BiCAT (Bidirectional Cross-Attention for Asynchronous Heterogeneous Multi-Source Trajectory Association), an end-to-end framework with bidirectional cross-attention for asynchronous, heterogeneous, multi-source association between active radar and infrared sensors. BiCAT dispenses with interpolation and dimensional pre-alignment by dynamically aligning in feature space. A dual-path, mask-aware attention module dynamically suppresses invalid or missing observations. A discriminative fusion classifier further enhances association robustness by jointly exploiting both similarity and divergence between sensor modalities. In crossing-trajectory scenarios, BiCAT attains 94% precision, outperforming SGFA by 9.3%; in parallel-queue scenarios, it achieves 92.6% recall, surpassing GCD-TA by 19.8%. These results demonstrate consistent gains in complex, high-density environments and provide reliable support for multi-source fusion.

title: Outsmarting AI cheats: Gradient-based game security using adversarial attacks
abstract: AI-driven visual cheats in competitive gaming—such as aimbots built on real-time object detectors—pose a growing threat to fair play that current anti-cheat systems fail to reliably address. This article presents a gradient-based adversarial attack methodology that neutralizes such cheats by generating Universal Adversarial Perturbations (UAPs) to suppress character detection without visibly degrading the game image. To achieve this, we first introduce a novel multi-game benchmark dataset of 10,000 annotated images (from CS2, Rust, Marvel Rivals, and Apex) to enable standardized evaluation. Building on this, we propose a UAP generation pipeline that utilizes Momentum Integrated Gradient (MIG) initialization to improve convergence and transferability across heterogeneous detection architectures. We further enhance this methodology with directional noise refinement and gradient filtering, which simultaneously improve attack effectiveness and preserve perceptual image quality. Finally, we introduce a zero-knowledge black-box perturbation search that operates without access to proxy models, relying solely on visual feedback. Extensive validation against real-world commercial cheats demonstrates that our approaches consistently outperform the existing Invisibility Cloak framework in both transferability and image fidelity.

title: Varying‐Distance Quantum Illumination Based on Quantum Memory
abstract: ABSTRACT Quantum illumination, leveraging inherent quantum correlations to maintain quantum enhancement in the lossy and noisy environment, provides a potential way for quantum radar. Although great progresses have been achieved, the distance of quantum illumination is fixed due to the employment of the fiber. In this work, the conditions of varying‐distance quantum illumination by using quantum memory are presented, where the idler beam storage can be on‐demand stored. This approach overcomes the fixed distance constraints and is tolerant to the storage noise. The quantum illumination conditions for targets at different distances can be implemented in the scenario with a controllable storage. This work offers a direct reference for potential practical applications of quantum illumination.

title: Privacy-Preserving Industrial Ergonomics: mmWave-Based Automated REBA Scoring and Pose Estimation
abstract: Work-related Musculoskeletal Disorders (WMSDs) require continuous ergonomic assessments. While Rapid Entire Body Assessment (REBA) is a gold-standard observation tool, manual monitoring is labor-intensive, and vision-based automation leads to privacy concerns. This paper proposes a novel end-to-end multi-task learning framework for privacy-preserving ergonomic assessment using millimetre-wave (mmWave) radar. A spatio-temporal backbone reconstructs 3D human skeletons, which serves as the biomechanical foundation for a subsequent regression head to generate REBA risk scores. To overcome the sparsity of radar point clouds, we utilise a multi-objective loss function incorporating biomechanical limits and temporal smoothness constraints. Furthermore, we implement an oversampling strategy to address the imbalance of high-risk postures in existing datasets. Experimental results on MMFi dataset demonstrate that our framework achieves a Categorical Accuracy of 77.78% and real-time performance with an inference latency of 5.70 ms. Our method reaches a High-risk REBA MAE of 0.93, which significantly outperforms both direct regression and two-stage pipelines in high-risk scenarios, providing a robust solution for non-invasive industrial ergonomic assessment.

title: Leakage Mobility and Passive Leakage Removal in Transmons with Tunable Couplers
abstract: Qubit leakage is a noticeable source of errors for quantum computing. In quantum processors, leakage excitations traveling between qubits generate correlated errors and perturb gate implementations. Leakage mobility can also be utilized for creating dedicated leakage removal pathways and removal units. To quantitatively characterize leakage mobility and to guide better design of processor architectures, we study here leakage dynamics in transmons with tunable couplers through numerical and analytical methods. Even if the couplers are tuned to cancel the single-excitation exchange or the ZZ interaction, the leakage hopping rates still persists in the range of 0.8-10 MHz due to transmon nonlinearity. In typical operation regimes, however, transmon frequency detuning localizes leakage excitations. The next-nearest-neighbor transmons can be still be near-resonant opening leakage tunneling channels. To suppress longer-range hopping, we find that the frequency spread of the next-nearest-neighbor transmons needs to be in the range of 1-4 MHz. Utilizing leakage mobility, we propose two passive leakage removal units. One is based on a tunable coupler and a pumped transmon, and another on a junction readout scheme. Based on realistic experimental parameters, our results on selectively mobilizing or localizing leakage excitations are readily applicable in superconducting quantum devices.

title: Attribute-Prompted Kernel Hashing for Unsupervised Data-Efficient Cross-Modal Retrieval
abstract: Unsupervised cross-modal hashing enables efficient retrieval of semantically related instances across different modalities without requiring manual semantic annotation. However, existing unsupervised methods rely heavily on large-scale image-text pairs. Collecting such data can be costly, particularly in scenarios where well-aligned pairs are scarce due to privacy and specialized constraints. More critically, existing methods tend to overfit to seen training data, restricting their generalization performance on unseen categories that the constrained training data cannot cover. To address these limitations, we propose Attribute-Prompted Kernel Hashing (APKH), a novel data-efficient approach that constructs a compact, modality-aligned Hamming space driven by the generalized attribute priors of vision-language foundation models. Specifically, APKH introduces two core modules: Context-optimized Attribute Kernel Mapping (CAKM) and Kernel-Smoothed Contrastive Alignment (KSCA). CAKM formulates cross-modal alignment through hyperspherical Radial Basis Function kernel mapping, optimizing dynamic attribute kernels via prompt learning to capture modality-invariant semantics. Furthermore, KSCA extends conventional point-to-point contrastive learning by modeling limited paired data as continuous kernel distributions. This explicit smoothing of the modality gap alleviates overfitting to sparse pairwise correlations. Extensive experiments demonstrate that APKH outperforms state-of-the-art hashing methods in the challenging cross-modal retrieval tasks from seen to unseen categories under data-constrained scenarios.

title: Extreme volume monogamy via bound-state engineering
abstract: Quantum steering ellipsoid (QSE) provides a faithful representation of a two-qubit state. When extended to tripartite systems, the steerability from a trusted party to different receivers is subject to volume monogamy relations, which only constrain the total steerability but cannot individually eliminate the steerability of an untrusted third party, leaving a potential channel for information leakage via steering. Here, we show that this residual steerability can be completely suppressed by selectively engineering bound states in local qubit-environment subsystems, without compromising the steerability between trusted parties. Specifically, when bound states are formed in the subsystems formed by the trusted parties and their environments but absent in the untrusted one, the untrusted party's QSE volume decays to zero, while the trusted party's QSE volume remains finite. Our results establish selective bound-state engineering as a mechanism for extreme volume monogamy, with potential applications in secure quantum communication with an untrusted third party.

title: Thinking While Speaking: Inference-Time Knowledge Transfer for Responsive and Intelligent Conversational Voice Agents
abstract: Voice agents face a fundamental tension: the reasoning, retrieval, and tool use that make foundation models capable are iterative and slow, while conversational interaction demands responses on a millisecond timescale. Smaller, real-time models meet the latency bar but cannot match foundation models on complex tasks, leaving current voice agents to trade away either responsiveness or capability. We introduce conversational infill, where a small talker model both immediately generates contextually grounded responses to hide the latency of an external reasoner model and fluently integrates streamed reasoner knowledge into its responses during inference. We curate a 290,571-example synthetic dataset spanning six domains and demonstrate that this task is learnable across seven widely used small language models ranging from 135M to 1.7B parameters. Our system implementation, ConvFill, sustains millisecond-level time-to-first-response while closing the accuracy gap to within 6.3% of the corresponding frontier reasoner performance. In a live user study (n=18) with talker deployments running on an Apple M2 SoC, participants rank ConvFill on par with frontier models overall, prefer it for retrieval-heavy tasks, and rate it significantly more responsive. These results show that conversational infill unlocks a new point on the latency-capability Pareto frontier, offering a practical path toward voice agents that are both responsive and highly capable. Code, models, and datasets are available at https://github.com/vysri/conversational-infill.

title: AutoML platform with adaptive explainability
abstract: El crecimiento exponencial en la generación y complejidad de los datos ha impulsado el desarrollo de técnicas avanzadas de aprendizaje automático capaces de extraer conocimiento útil de manera eficiente. En este contexto, el aprendizaje automático automatizado (AutoML) emerge como una alternativa que simplifica y democratiza el uso de estos métodos al automatizar tareas tradicionalmente complejas, como la selección, el entrenamiento y la optimización de modelos. Este Trabajo de Fin de Grado presenta el desarrollo de una plataforma web inteligente basada en AutoML, concretamente mediante el uso de AutoGluon, orientada a facilitar la creación y explotación de modelos predictivos. La propuesta incorpora un enfoque centrado en el usuario, permitiendo adaptar tanto la interacción como la explicación de los resultados en función de su nivel de conocimiento en inteligencia artificial. De este modo, se busca mejorar la accesibilidad y la interpretabilidad de los sistemas de aprendizaje automático. La solución desarrollada pone especial énfasis en usuarios no expertos, eliminando barreras técnicas y promoviendo una experiencia intuitiva mediante interfaces adaptativas y mecanismos de explicación personalizados. Los resultados obtenidos evidencian la viabilidad de este enfoque, demostrando que es posible combinar automatización, usabilidad e interpretabilidad en una única herramienta que facilite tanto el uso como la comprensión de modelos de aprendizaje automático.

title: Effects of AI-Driven Customer Service on Customer Loyalty Among Mobile Fintech Users in Calabar, Nigeria
abstract: This study examined the effect of AI-driven customer service on customer loyalty among users of mobile FinTech service providers in Calabar, Cross River State, Nigeria. Specifically, it assessed the influence of AI chatbot, personalized service experience, quick service automation, and AI security infrastructure on customer loyalty. The study adopted a cross-sectional survey research design. A sample size of 357 respondents was determined using the Topman sample size determination procedure from an indeterminate population of mobile FinTech users, while purposive sampling was employed to select respondents who had actively used mobile FinTech platforms for at least one year. Data were collected from 342 valid respondents using a structured five-point Likert-scale questionnaire and analysed using descriptive statistics and multiple linear regression analysis in SPSS. The regression model was statistically significant (F = 78.245, p < 0.001) and explained 48.2% of the variation in customer loyalty (R² = 0.482). AI chatbot emerged as the strongest predictor of customer loyalty (β = 0.677, p < 0.001), followed by AI security infrastructure (β = 0.479, p < 0.001), personalized service experience (β = 0.337, p = 0.010), and quick service automation (β = 0.170, p < 0.001). The findings demonstrate that AI-driven customer service significantly enhances customer loyalty towards mobile FinTech service providers. The study concludes that effective deployment of AI-driven customer service represents an important strategy for strengthening customer loyalty within the mobile FinTech industry. Accordingly, mobile FinTech service providers should enhance AI chatbot capabilities, strengthen AI-based security systems, improve service personalization, and optimize automated service delivery to promote sustained customer engagement and loyalty in Nigeria's competitive FinTech environment.

title: BRAÇO PESCADOR ROBÓTICO COMO ESTRATÉGIA PEDAGÓGICA PARA TRABALHAR MOTRICIDADE E ROBÓTICA COM CRIANÇAS
abstract: O ensino precisa evoluir de uma prática em que os alunos são agentes passivos, para outra que os tornem participantes ativos na construção do seu conhecimento. As práticas lúdicas, por serem mais atrativas, facilitam o aprendizado. Assim, a robótica educacional, no desenvolvimento de projetos com aplicação pedagógica, promove o aprendizado de conteúdos de diversas áreas, de forma lúdica, através da experimentação. Esta pesquisa teve como objetivo o desenvolvimento de um Braço Pescador Robótico que utiliza componentes tecnológicos relacionadas à robótica educacional para promover um maior engajamento dos estudantes, desenvolvendo especificamente a motricidade fina de mãos e dedos. Neste sentido, está sendo utilizado em duas escolas da rede municipal de Santa Maria-RS. As escolas de ensino fundamental foram escolhidas para utilizá-lo em diferentes aplicações, com base no currículo e planejamento das professoras. Em uma escola, turma de 1º ano, em outra, pré-escola, 1º e 2º anos. No desenvolvimento das experiências com os alunos, criaram-se novas possibilidades de utilização do Braço Pescador Robótico, no aprendizado de diferentes conteúdos.

title: PRISM benchmarks
abstract: The evaluation is conducted over various benchmark KGs. The French Royalty KG is fully curated from DBpedia and comprises contextual information about several biologically connected French royal members. YAGO3-10 is a subset of YAGO3, containing entities with a minimum of 10 relations each. YAGO3-10 contains the triples describing personal characteristics such as citizenship, gender, and profession. The DB100K benchmark extracted from DBpedia portrays numerous entities with hierarchical relationships (e.g., dbo:book/dbo:author). FB15K-237 is an extensive knowledge base derived from Freebase that represents information on sports, movies, bands, music, etc. FB15K-237 discards duplicate relations to avoid data leakage issues and to enhance the performance of the KG completion task.

title: Kryptos K4: A Structural Investigation
abstract: Abstract This paper presents the findings of an independent structural investigation conducted on June 16, 2026 by the JVE Research & Innovation team. Kryptos, the encrypted sculpture installed at CIA headquarters in Langley, Virginia in 1990, contains four panels. Three were broken in the 1990s. The fourth, K4, resisted all public attacks for thirty-five years before its plaintext was accidentally recovered from a Smithsonian archive in September 2025 discovered, not solved. abstract: 现有一阶梯度、拟牛顿、元启发式优化方法存在适用场景割裂、高维病态收敛能力不足、缺少统一数学理论支撑等问题。依托《易经》错卦、综卦对称数理关系,本文构建D维卦象代数空间,定义两类基础对称变换算子,搭建GUO统一优化理论体系。完整给出卦群代数证明、广义正交投影分步推导、收敛引理与定理全过程演算;基于卦变换设计GUO-QN、GUO-SGD、GUO-MO、GUO-Discrete、GUO-NAS五类理论算法,迭代公式全部采用单行线性写法,杜绝复制分式乱码;配套迭代异常判定对照表、GRPO在线超参调度完整推导。全文仅做纯理论数学推演,无仿真实验、无虚构测试数据,全套推导、伪代码、表格完整留存,可直接作为理论论文底稿。Traditional first-order gradient, quasi-Newton and metaheuristic optimization algorithms are separated in applicable scenarios and lack sufficient convergence performance for high-dimensional ill-conditioned problems, as well as unified mathematical support. Based on the symmetrical mathematical logic of wrong hexagram and inverted hexagram in I Ching, this paper constructs D-dimensional hexagram algebraic space, defines two basic symmetric transformation operators, and establishes the GUO unified optimization theoretical system. This paper provides full step-by-step derivation of hexagram group, generalized orthogonal projection, convergence lemmas and theorems. Five theoretical algorithms GUO-QN, GUO-SGD, GUO-MO, GUO-Discrete, GUO-NAS are proposed with all formulas written in single-line linear format to avoid garbled text after copying. Complete iteration fault table and GRPO hyperparameter derivation are attached. This paper only contains pure mathematical deduction without simulation and fabricated experimental data, with all derivations, pseudocode and tables retained completely.

title: Finite Consequence Formation: A Release-Validity Criterion for Finite Intelligence
abstract: This record fixes the public release of an 8-page preprint on Finite Consequence Formation. The paper states a release-validity criterion for finite intelligence: before a finite system releases a prediction, proof, diagnosis, scientific claim, control decision, or action as warranted, its finite contact with reality must be structurally sufficient to carry the declared consequence. For a reality space R, a finite contact map C:R->X, and a declared consequence Q:R->Y, the exact release-validity gate is K_C subset K_Q. Equivalently, Q factors through contact, Q=Qbar after C. When the gate fails, a contact cell carries non-flat consequence load, Lambda_{C,Q}(x)=Q(C^{-1}(x)), and forced answering is not a valid substitute for the missing required distinction. The record also includes the static hidden-twin load-repair flagship: the original C+-contact graph has 85/1099 obstructions and the full same-cell graph has 110/1437 obstructions; a deterministic lawful splitter using only frozen C+ contact coordinates reduces both obstruction counts to zero. Six forced-answer systems fail, and 512 random nuisance binary splits never clear all obstructions. This is a static release/repair result, not a dynamic action-CREATE claim.

title: An Improved SMOTE Algorithm Based on Label-Smoothing Generation
abstract: Imbalanced data classification is a challenging problem in the fields of machine learning and data mining. The Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) is a widely used over-sampling method that addresses this issue by linearly interpolating between minority class samples. However, traditional SMOTE assigns absolute hard labels to all synthetic samples, neglecting the ambiguity and uncertainty inherent in boundary regions, which often leads to overfitting and high sensitivity to noise. To overcome these limitations, this paper proposes an improved SMOTE algorithm based on label-smoothing generation, termed LSG-SMOTE. Instead of assigning a rigid binary label to newly generated samples, the proposed algorithm analyzes the local neighborhood structure of the seed samples in the feature space and dynamically generates a continuous label distribution (soft labels) for each synthetic sample. This soft label reflects the blending degree of minority and majority classes in that local region, introducing a regularization effect during the training process. A soft-label cross-entropy loss function is further incorporated to train the classification models, forcing the classifier to build smoother and more robust decision boundaries. The theoretical framework of LSG-SMOTE provides a novel perspective on over-sampling by bridging the gap between feature-space synthesis and label-space smoothing, effectively enhancing the generalization capability of classifiers on skewed data distributions.
